subtopics.title: Why VAT Exists and How It Works

questions.question: VAT is best described as:
options: An INDIRECT tax on consumption — paid by the final consumer, collected and paid over by businesses
A direct tax on business profits
A levy on employees' wages
A tax on imports only

questions.question: Output tax and input tax are, respectively:
options: Tax on imports and tax on exports
VAT charged on what the vendor SELLS, and VAT reclaimed on what the vendor BUYS
VAT on assets and VAT on expenses
The standard rate and the zero rate

questions.question: The bakery buying flour at R100 and selling bread at R160 hands SARS the tax on:
options: R160 — the full selling price
R100 — the purchase price
R60 — the value it added, being output tax less input tax
Nothing — bread is always zero-rated

questions.question: On the INVOICE basis, VAT is recorded:
options: Only when the debtor pays
At the end of the financial year
When stock is delivered to the shop
When the invoice is issued, whether or not payment has happened

questions.question: Zero-rated supplies include:
options: Brown bread, maize meal, rice, samp, dried beans, milk, eggs, fresh fruit and vegetables, vegetable oil, paraffin — and exports
Residential rent and bank interest
Restaurant meals and clothing
School fees and bus fares

questions.question: Exempt supplies include:
options: Maize meal and eggs
Financial services on which interest is charged, residential rent, public road and rail transport, and educational services
Exported goods
Fuel-powered deliveries

questions.question: The test that separates zero-rated from exempt is:
options: Whether the item is food
Whether the price is above R100
Whether the SUPPLIER may claim its input tax — zero-rated is taxable at nought so inputs ARE recoverable; exempt is outside the system so they are NOT
Whether the customer is registered

questions.question: A vendor selling only zero-rated goods will typically:
options: Pay a large amount to SARS each period
Charge VAT at the standard rate anyway
Be unable to register for VAT
RECEIVE A REFUND — no output tax is charged while input tax on purchases is still reclaimed

questions.question: Goods are priced at R2 000 excluding VAT (rate 15%). The inclusive price is:
options: R2 300 — R2 000 plus VAT of R300, or R2 000 × 1,15

questions.question: A till slip totals R2 300 INCLUDING VAT. The VAT portion is:
options: R345 — fifteen percent of R2 300
R230 — ten percent of the total

questions.question: Stock costs R1 200, the mark-up is 50% on cost, and VAT is 15%. The price the customer pays is:
options: R1 380 — cost plus VAT, then mark-up
R1 800 — no VAT is added to marked-up goods
R2 070 — mark up to R1 800 first, then add VAT

questions.question: Where input tax exceeds output tax for the period, the vendor:
options: Pays the difference to SARS
Ignores the difference
Carries the whole amount as an expense
Is REFUNDABLE by SARS — the return produces a claim rather than a payment

questions.question: When a customer returns goods, the vendor:
options: Issues a CREDIT NOTE showing the VAT portion and reduces output tax accordingly
Keeps the output tax already declared
Claims the full selling price as input tax
Adjusts nothing until year end

questions.question: When a debtor's account is written off as irrecoverable on the invoice basis:
options: The output tax already paid over is simply lost
The VAT portion of the written-off debt may be CLAIMED BACK as input tax — and must be declared again if the debtor later pays
The whole debt is claimed as input tax
VAT is unaffected by bad debts

questions.question: VAT collected from customers is best described as:
options: Additional revenue of the business
A discount on purchases
TRUST MONEY — the state's money held by the vendor until the return is due
A loan from SARS

questions.question: The internal auditor's searching test on input tax claims is:
options: Was the amount under R1 000?
Was the supplier a large company?
Was the claim made before month end?
Does every claim rest on a VALID TAX INVOICE for a genuine BUSINESS purpose?

subtopics.title: The Line at the Bottom of the Slip

questions.question: The shop that charges you VAT:
options: Is a COLLECTOR, not an owner — it holds the money and hands it to SARS
Keeps the VAT as extra profit
Pays the VAT out of its own profits
Splits the VAT with the supplier

questions.question: Adding all the businesses' payments along the bread chain gives:
options: Three separate taxes on the same bread
Exactly the tax on what the final consumer paid — each business taxed only on its own slice of value
More tax than the consumer paid
Nothing, since bread is exempt

questions.question: What a registered business actually pays over each period is:
options: All the VAT it collected
Fifteen percent of its profit
The DIFFERENCE between what it collected and what it was charged
A fixed monthly amount

subtopics.title: The Three Baskets at the Till

questions.question: The essentials basket is zero-rated because:
options: A tax on food hits a poor household far harder — a family spending most of its income on food would pay most of its income in tax
Food is cheap to produce
Farmers refuse to charge VAT
Fresh goods spoil quickly

questions.question: Exports sit in the zero-rated basket because:
options: Exporters are exempt from all taxes
The goods will be consumed in another country, which taxes them instead
Export prices are always low
Foreign buyers cannot pay VAT

questions.question: The landlord renting out flats charges no VAT and:
options: Claims back the VAT on paint and repairs
Charges VAT on repairs instead
Gets NOTHING back on what he paid — exempt supplies mean the input tax is simply absorbed
Receives a refund from SARS each period

questions.question: Brown bread is zero-rated while a fancy seed loaf is not, showing that:
options: The list changes weekly
Bakers choose their own rates
All bread is exempt
The list protects STAPLES, not shopping preferences

subtopics.title: The Fifteen-on-One-Fifteen Trick, and Whose Money It Is

questions.question: The slogan for the two directions is:
options: Going up, fifteen on a hundred; coming down, fifteen on a hundred and fifteen
Fifteen percent both ways
Divide by fifteen going up, multiply going down
Always take fifteen percent of the total

questions.question: Taking fifteen percent of an inclusive R2 300 gives R345, which is wrong because:
options: The rate is actually fourteen percent
The fifteen percent was calculated on the SMALLER pre-tax price — R2 300 is already 115 parts
R2 300 includes a discount
VAT is never calculated on totals

questions.question: On stock costing R1 200 sold at R2 070 inclusive, the R270 of VAT is:
options: Part of the shop's profit
A discount to the customer
SARS's money sitting in the till until the return is due — the profit is the R600 mark-up
The supplier's commission

questions.question: Charging customers "VAT" while not registered is:
options: Allowed for small businesses
A minor administrative oversight
Permitted if the money is later paid over
Simply theft from the customer, who believes the money is going to SARS
